title: 25 April
summary: Units led by the Armed Forces Movement — a clandestine organisation of middle-ranking officers formed over the previous year around the colonial war and a grievance about promotions — left barracks in the early hours of 25 April 1974 on a plan drawn up by Otelo Saraiva de Carvalho, and held Lisbon by the morning. Marcelo Caetano surrendered at the Carmo barracks that afternoon and insisted on handing power to General António de Spínola, whom the movement had not chosen but accepted as a figurehead. Crowds ignored the broadcast instruction to stay indoors, and the carnations put into gun barrels gave the day its name; the only deaths were of civilians shot by the political police outside its Lisbon headquarters. The coup itself was over within a day, but it opened nineteen months in which the form of the new regime, the ownership of the economy and the future of the African territories were all undecided. It is the pivot of this part of the atlas: most of what follows descends from it.
